findings.title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts
findings.body: When a slot falls on a date with an override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before evaluating the host's busy intervals. An override defines working availability; it does not make existing bookings or calendar events available. Consequently, both fixed and round-robin hosts can be offered for slots that conflict with existing commitments. Accepted override slots must still pass the busy-time check.

findings.title: Override validation accepts partially overlapping slots
findings.body: The override checks only reject slots ending before the override starts or starting after it ends. They do not require the entire event to fit inside the override, and even a slot starting exactly at the override's end passes. For example, a fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override is considered available for a 10:30–11:30 event generated from another host's availability. Require full containment within an override interval before considering the host available.

findings.title: Working-hours validation rejects valid split schedules
findings.body: The workingHours.find predicate rejects a slot if it is outside any working interval for the weekday, rather than accepting it if it fits one interval. With ordinary split availability of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected for being outside the afternoon interval, and a 14:00 slot is rejected for being outside the morning interval. This removes all available slots for such hosts. Validate membership in at least one applicable interval instead; a weekday with no applicable intervals should also be unavailable.

findings.title: Working-hours end check uses the slot start time
findings.body: The end variable is calculated from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime. This lets events extend past a host's working-hours boundary as long as their start is inside it. In particular, when another host's date override generates additional candidates, a fixed host working until 11:00 can pass this check for a 10:30–11:30 event. Compare the actual event end against the working interval's end.

findings.title: Timezone conversion drops overrides that cross attendee midnight
findings.body: The converted override endpoints are reduced to hour/minute values, discarding their dates. An override from 22:00–23:00 UTC viewed in UTC+1 becomes startTime 1380 and endTime 0. buildSlots treats that as an invalid range and produces no slots, although 23:00–00:00 is valid availability. Preserve the converted day boundaries and split ranges at attendee midnight instead of wrapping the end back to zero.
